en: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Abi Umar's—they said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: No one asked the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about the Dajjal more than I asked him about him. He said to me: "O my little son, what makes you weary regarding him? He will not harm you." He said: I said: "They claim that with him are rivers of water and mountains of bread." He said: "He is too insignificant to Allah for that."

Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Ghubari narrated to us: Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Abu Uthman, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to me: "O my little son."

Abu al-Rabi' Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Ataki narrated to us: Abd al-Warith narrated to us: Abu al-Tayyah narrated to us: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us (H). And Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us—and the wording is his: Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was the best of people in character. I had a brother called Abu Umayr—he said: I think he said—he was a weaned child—he said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came and saw him, he would say: "O Abu Umayr, what did the Nughayr (little sparrow) do?" He said: And he used to play with it.

Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Tamimi and Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated to me, they said: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us: Muhammad—namely Ibn Mutarrif Abu Ghassan—narrated to us: Abu Hazim narrated to me, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: Al-Mundhir ibn Abi Usayd was brought to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) when he was born, and the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) placed him on his thigh while Abu Usayd was sitting. Then the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) became occupied with something in front of him, so Abu Usayd ordered his son to be carried away from the thigh of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and they took him back. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) turned his attention back and said: "Where is the infant?" Abu Usayd said: "We took him home, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "What is his name?" He said: "So-and-so, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "No, but rather his name is al-Mundhir." So he named him al-Mundhir on that day.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aisha, who said: We brought Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) for him to perform tahnik for him, so we looked for a date, and finding it proved difficult for us.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Hisham—meaning Ibn Urwah—narrated to us, from his father, from Aisha, that young boys used to be brought to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and he would invoke blessings upon them and perform tahnik for them.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Ali ibn Mushir, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Asma' bint Abi Bakr, that she migrated to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) while she was pregnant with Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr. And he mentioned the like of the hadith of Abu Usamah.

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-Ala' narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Asma', that she became pregnant with Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr in Mecca. She said: I set out while at full term, and I arrived in Medina and stopped at Quba', and I gave birth to him at Quba'. Then I came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he placed him in his lap. Then he called for a date, chewed it, and spat a little into his mouth; so the first thing to enter his belly was the saliva of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). Then he performed tahnik for him with the date, then prayed for him and invoked blessings upon him. And he was the first newborn born in Islam.

Al-Hakam ibn Musa Abu Salih narrated to us: Shu'ayb—meaning Ibn Ishaq—narrated to us: Hisham ibn Urwah informed me: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and Fatimah bint al-Mundhir ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me that they said: Asma' bint Abi Bakr set out when she migrated while she was pregnant with Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr. She arrived in Quba' and gave birth to Abd Allah at Quba'. Then, when she had given birth, she went to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) so that he would perform tahnik for him. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) took him from her and placed him in his lap. Then he called for a date. He said: Aisha said: We spent some time searching for it before we found it. Then he chewed it and spat it into his mouth, so the first thing that entered his stomach was indeed the saliva of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). Then Asma' said: Then he stroked him, prayed for him, and named him Abd Allah. Later, when he was seven or eight years old, he came to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), al-Zubayr having ordered him to do that. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) smiled when he saw him coming toward him, and then accepted his pledge of allegiance.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Allah ibn Barrad al-Ash'ari, and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, they said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: A boy was born to me, so I brought him to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he named him Ibrahim and performed tahnik for him with a date.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Khirash narrated to us: Amr ibn Asim narrated to us: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us: Thabit narrated to us: Anas ibn Malik narrated to me, he said: A son of Abu Talhah died; and he recounted the hadith the like of it.

Muhammad ibn Hatim ibn Maymun narrated to me: Bahz narrated to us: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: A son of Abu Talhah from Umm Sulaym died, so she said to her family: "Do not tell Abu Talhah about his son until I tell him myself." He said: So he came, and she brought him his dinner, and he ate and drank. He said: Then she beautified herself for him in the best manner she ever had before that, and he had intercourse with her. When she saw that he was satisfied and had had relations with her, she said: "O Abu Talhah, tell me, if some people lend something on loan to the people of a household and then ask for their loan back, do they have the right to withhold it from them?" He said: "No." She said: "Then seek reward for your son." He said: So he became angry and said: "You left me until I defiled myself, then informed me about my son!" He went until he came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and told him what had happened. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "May Allah bless you both in your night that has passed." He said: So she conceived. He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was on a journey, and she was with him. Whenever the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came to Medina from a journey, he would not enter it by night. As they drew near to Medina, labor pains overtook her, so Abu Talhah was held back with her, while the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) proceeded on. He said: Abu Talhah said: "You know, O Lord, that it pleases me to leave with Your Messenger when he leaves and enter with him when he enters, and I have been held back by what You see." He said: Umm Sulaym said: "O Abu Talhah, I no longer feel what I was feeling; proceed." So we proceeded. He said: And labor pains overtook her when they arrived, and she gave birth to a boy. My mother said to me: "O Anas, let no one breastfeed him until you take him in the morning to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." When morning came, I carried him and went with him to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). He said: I found him with a branding iron in his hand. When he saw me, he said: "Perhaps Umm Sulaym has given birth?" I said: "Yes." So he put down the branding iron. He said: And I brought the boy and placed him in his lap. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) called for an Ajwah date of Medina, chewed it in his mouth until it was soft, and then put it into the child's mouth, and the child began licking it. He said: Thereupon the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Look at the love of the Ansar for dates!" He said: Then he wiped his face and named him Abd Allah.
Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Hammad ibn Mas'adah narrated to us: Ibn Awn narrated to us, from Muhammad, from Anas, with this story, similar to the hadith of Yazid.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Ibn Awn informed us, from Ibn Sirin, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: A son of Abu Talhah was ill. Abu Talhah went out, and the boy passed away. When Abu Talhah returned, he said: "How is my son?" Umm Sulaym said: "He is calmer than he was." She served him dinner and he ate dinner, then had relations with her. When he had finished, she said: "Bury the boy." When morning came, Abu Talhah went to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and informed him. He said: "Did you act as bride and groom last night?" He said: "Yes." He said: "O Allah, bless them both." So she gave birth to a boy. Abu Talhah said to me: "Carry him until you bring him to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." So he brought him to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and she sent some dates with him. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) took him and said: "Is there anything with him?" They said: "Yes, dates." The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) took them and chewed them, then took them from his mouth and placed them into the mouth of the boy, then rubbed his palate (performed tahnik) and named him Abd Allah.

Abd al-A'la ibn Hammad narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: I took Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah al-Ansari to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) when he was born, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was in a wool cloak smearing tar on a camel of his. He said: "Do you have any dates with you?" I said: "Yes." So I handed him some dates, and he put them into his mouth and chewed them, then opened the mouth of the baby and spat them into his mouth. The child began licking it, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The love of the Ansar for dates!" And he named him Abd Allah.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—and he mentioned several hadiths, among them: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The man most provoking Allah's wrath on the Day of Resurrection, the vilest, and the one provoking the greatest anger upon him, is a man who was named King of Kings; there is no King except Allah."

Sa'id ibn Amr al-Ash'athi, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us—and the wording is Ahmad's; al-Ash'athi said: informed us, and the other two said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Indeed, the most vile name before Allah is a man named King of Kings." Ibn Abi Shaybah added in his narration: "There is no Sovereign except Allah, Mighty and Majestic." Al-Ash'athi said: Sufyan said: like Shahan Shah. And Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: I asked Abu Amr about 'akhna'' and he said: "the most lowly (awda')."

Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata', who said: I named my daughter Barrah, so Zaynab bint Abi Salamah said to me: "The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade this name. I was named Barrah, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: Do not claim purity for yourselves; Allah knows best who the righteous among you are." They said: "What should we name her?" He said: "Name her Zaynab."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to me: Isa ibn Yunus informed us (H). And Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us; both said: al-Walid ibn Kathir narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata' narrated to me: Zaynab bint Umm Salamah narrated to me, she said: My name was Barrah, so the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) named me Zaynab. She said: And Zaynab bint Jahsh entered upon him and her name was Barrah, so he named her Zaynab.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Ata' ibn Abi Maymunah: I heard Abu Rafi' narrating from Abu Hurayrah (H). And Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Ata' ibn Abi Maymunah, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, that Zaynab's name was Barrah, and it was said: "She purifies herself." So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) named her Zaynab. And the wording of the hadith belongs to these narrators other than Ibn Bashshar. And Ibn Abi Shaybah said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us from Shu'bah.

Amr al-Naqid and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us—and the wording is Amr's—they said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, the freed slave of the family of Talhah, from Kurayb, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Juwayriyah's name was Barrah, so the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) changed her name to Juwayriyah, and he disliked that it should be said: "He went out from Barrah (piety)." And in the hadith of Ibn Abi Umar, from Kurayb, he said: "I heard Ibn Abbas."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ubayd Allah, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, that a daughter of Umar was called Asiyah (disobedient), so the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) named her Jamilah (beautiful).

Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Zuhayr ibn Harb, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id, and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ubayd Allah: Nafi' informed me, from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) changed the name of Asiyah (disobedient) and said: "You are Jamilah (beautiful)." Ahmad said 'from' in place of 'informed me.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to us: Rawh narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah say: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) intended to forbid naming someone Ya'la, Barakah, Aflah, Yasar, Nafi', and the like; then I saw that he remained silent about it afterward and did not say anything. Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) passed away without having forbidden that. Then Umar intended to forbid that, but then abandoned it.

And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Jarir informed me (H). And Umayyah ibn Bistam narrated to me: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us: Rawh—and he is Ibn al-Qasim—narrated to us (H). And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us; all of them from Mansur with the chain of Zuhayr. As for the hadith of Jarir and Rawh, it is like the hadith of Zuhayr with its story. As for the hadith of Shu'bah, it contains only the mention of naming the boy, and he did not mention the four words.

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Mansur narrated to us, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, from Rabi' ibn Umaylah, from Samurah ibn Jundab, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The dearest of speech to Allah are four: Subhan Allah (Glory be to Allah), al-Hamdu lillah (Praise be to Allah), La ilaha illa Allah (There is no god but Allah), and Allahu Akbar (Allah is the Greatest). It does not matter with which of them you begin. And do not name your boy Yasar, nor Rabah, nor Najih, nor Aflah; for you might ask, \"Is he there?\" and he might not be there, so one would say, \"No.\"" They are only four, so do not add more upon me.

And Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabi', from his father, from Samurah ibn Jundab, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Do not name your boy Rabah, nor Yasar, nor Aflah, nor Nafi'."

Yahya ibn Yahya and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us; Abu Bakr said: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Rukayn, from his father, from Samurah; and Yahya said: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman informed us, he said: I heard al-Rukayn narrating from his father, from Samurah ibn Jundab, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade us from naming our slaves with four names: Aflah, Rabah, Yasar, and Nafi'.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr, Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-Anazi narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Numayr's—they said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from his father, from Simak ibn Harb, from Alqamah ibn Wa'il, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: When I arrived in Najran, they questioned me and said: "Indeed, you recite: 'O sister of Aaron' [Surah Maryam 19:28], while Moses lived such-and-such long before Jesus." When I came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), I asked him about that, and he said: "Indeed, they used to name their people after their prophets and righteous people who came before them."

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Amr al-Naqid, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, they said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah saying: Abu al-Qasim (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Name yourselves with my name, but do not take my kunyah (Abu al-Qasim)." Amr said: "from Abu Hurayrah," and did not say "I heard."
